posts.topic: Independent second-look audit with already-known findings and credits excluded
posts.original_media_alt: Branded RETALLY audit-controls graphic: A discrepancy is not a recovery, with a four-stage evidence and authorization pathway.
posts.original_caption:
Already have a freight auditor? That's not a problem. It's the starting point.

A useful second look should find what's still unresolved—not take credit for somebody else's work.

Before calling an invoice issue "new," reconcile:
• Previous audit findings
• Carrier corrections and automatic credits
• Open disputes and approved claims
• Rebill chains for the same shipment

Only a supported, unaddressed discrepancy belongs in the next conversation.

RETALLY offers a $0-upfront initial Second-Look Recovery Audit for agreed eligible scope. Recovery work is separately authorized in writing; outcomes are not guaranteed.

posts.topic: Two invoices, one shipment; investigate corrections, credit-and-rebill
posts.original_media_alt: RETALLY evidence ledger separates a flagged discrepancy, supported evidence, customer authorization, and actual funds or credits received.
posts.original_caption:
TWO INVOICES. ONE SHIPMENT.

Is that duplicate billing?

Not necessarily.

A corrected invoice, credit-and-rebill, or replacement bill can look like a duplicate until you trace the actual charges and credits.

Before flagging it:
01 / Match the shipment or PRO number
02 / Check original versus corrected bills
03 / Reconcile payments and credit memos

A suspicious pattern isn't automatically an overpayment. An overpayment isn't automatically a recovery.
